newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-PM sees 1998 Russian inflation 5-8 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-PM sees 1998 Russian inflation 5-8 pct.

text.p: Russian inflation is likely to be 5-8 percent in 1998, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin told senior finance ministry officials on Tuesday.

The government has targeted inflation of about 12 percent year-on-year in December this year, down from 21.8 percent in 1996. The monthly price increase in April was 1.0 percent, giving a record low year-on-year increase of 15.3 percent.
Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais told the meeting that the government would be targeting the lower end of the range.
"Of course, we shall be aiming for the tougher parameter -- five percent," said Chubais, who is also First Deputy Prime Minister in charge of economic policy.
Chubais repeated government forecasts that gross domestic product would rise two percent in 1998.
